identificationModule.briefTitle: Impact of Metformin on Immuno-virologic Parameters in HIV
identificationModule.officialTitle: A 72 Week, Randomized, Open-label vs Observation Study to Assess the Potential Immuno-virologic Benefit of Metformin in HIV-infected Individuals Receiving Antiretroviral Therapy

statusModule.whyStopped: During the COVID pandemic, our IRB halted enrollment into the study among other changes. Post COVID it was decided that too long an interval between patient enrollment was problematic for the study and a discussion was made to terminate.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Non-diabetic, aviremic HIV-infected individuals on antiretroviral therapy (ART) will be randomized to metformin therapy or to observation for 72 weeks. Primary objective is to assess change over 72 weeks in CD4 T cell negative checkpoint receptors (PD-1 and TIGIT). The study will also explore the 72 week impact of metformin on change in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) as a surrogate marker of atherosclerosis, on neuropsychological (NP) performance, strength, and change in body composition.

interventions.name: Metformin
interventions.description: Metformin 500 mg Extended Release (ER) qd increasing to 1000 mg ER qd at week 4 and continued to week 48.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Percentage of CD4 T Cells Expressing PD1+TIGIT+

identificationModule.briefTitle: Neurofeedback During Naturalistic Stimuli to Reduce Craving in Heroin Addiction
identificationModule.officialTitle: Brain-to-brain Neurofeedback During Naturalistic Dynamic Stimuli to Reduce Craving in Heroin Addiction

leadSponsor.name: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Support groups are an important component of addiction treatment, where individuals at more stable stages of their recovery help others by sharing personal experiences. This phenomenon suggests that the brain states of individuals further along in their recovery process may be useful in guiding those who are at an earlier stage. In this project, the researchers will test this idea and develop a personalized therapeutic tool based on real-time fMRI neurofeedback, whereby individuals with heroin use disorder (iHUD) early in treatment will learn to modulate their own brain state to more closely align with iHUD who are at later stages of treatment. Specifically, iHUD exhibit heightened reactivity to naturalistic drug cues in brain networks underlying salience attribution, reward processing, executive function and others. interventions.name: Real-time fMRI Neurofeedback
interventions.description: Real-time feedback reflecting the similarity between participant's brain activity patterns and a predefined target while viewing a drug-related movie.

interventions.name: Sham Real-time fMRI Neurofeedback
interventions.description: Real-time feedback yoked to another participant and not reflective of the participant's own brain activity.

identificationModule.briefTitle: Development and Evaluation of a PrEP Decision Aid for Women Seeking Domestic Violence Services in Baltimore
identificationModule.officialTitle: Development and Evaluation of a PrEP Decision Aid for Women Seeking Domestic Violence Services in Baltimore

leadSponsor.name: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study is designed to develop and test an individual decision aid for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) tailored to Black women who have been exposed to intimate partner violence and are working with a domestic violence service provider. three different ways of delivering the tailored decision aid are being tested: 1) as an individual tool; or 2) as a shared decision-making tool with a domestic violence advocate; as compared to generalized information. The goal of decision aid will be to address key cultural and structural factors affecting these women and can help them gain PrEP awareness and access.

interventions.name: Individual PrEP Decision Aid
interventions.description: Participant engages with the decision support tool designed to optimize PrEP uptake among Black cisgender women who have experienced IPV independently. They also enter data independently.

interventions.name: CDC PrEP Video
interventions.description: A video from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that provides basic, general information on PrEP

interventions.name: Shared PrEP Decision Aid
interventions.description: Domestic violence service advocate (DVA) engages with the decision support tool designed to optimize PrEP uptake among Black cisgender women who have experienced IPV with the participant and enters data
